Tell us what feels wrong in the space.

A few useful details can make the first conversation faster and clearer.

Start with the problem

You do not need to diagnose the building before calling. Tell us what you notice. A room may feel drafty. An upper floor may stay warm. A floor above a crawl space or garage may feel cold.

Explain when the problem is strongest. Winter wind, summer humidity, heavy rain, and sudden temperature changes can reveal different air paths.

Share the age and type of property. A central Belleville home may have several renovation layers. A newer addition may have a difficult wall connection. A workshop may have large doors and an exposed roof line.

Information that helps

Tell us whether framing is open or covered. Mention current electrical, plumbing, roofing, or renovation work. Timing can affect when spray foam should be installed.

Always share known moisture history. Roof leaks, wet foundation areas, plumbing failures, staining, or musty odours should be reviewed. Spray foam should not hide an active problem.

Photos can help us understand access. Wide views show the full assembly. Close views show framing joints or service openings. Do not enter an unsafe space to take a photo.

What happens after you contact us

We review the details and follow up using the phone number or email you provide. We may ask a few questions about access, surfaces, and project timing.

If a site estimate makes sense, we arrange the next step. The goal is to define a specific treatment area. We also identify preparation or repairs that should happen before installation.

An estimate should be understandable. It should describe the work area, not only a number. Ask about coverage, protection, ventilation, curing, safe re-entry, and coordination with other trades.

Call for a faster response

For a direct conversation, call (613) 912-7508. If we cannot answer immediately, leave your name, number, and a short description of the space.

Belleville Spray Foam Insulation serves local homeowners, builders, renovators, landlords, and commercial property managers. We discuss attics, walls, crawl spaces, garage transitions, shops, and new construction.

Your privacy

The contact form collects only the details needed to respond to your request. Information is sent to the business lead sheet and used for project follow-up.

Do not send banking details, government numbers, or other sensitive information. Project photos should avoid showing private documents or unrelated personal items.

Submitting a form does not create a contract. It begins a conversation about the property and the possible next step.

Before installation day

If you move forward after an estimate, we review preparation for the selected area. Stored items may need to move. Fixed finishes and equipment may need protection. Access routes should be clear and safe.

Tell us if site conditions change. A new leak, plumbing issue, or construction delay can affect the schedule. It is better to pause than to cover a condition that still needs attention.

Coordinate other trades early. Wiring, pipes, framing, and roof repairs may need completion before spray foam. Drywall and finish work normally happen after curing and the planned review.

Helpful questions for your first call

Ask which surface may be treated and why. Ask how that area connects with the rest of the wall, roof, or floor. Ask whether any part needs further investigation.

Ask what must be removed, covered, or kept accessible. Ask about ventilation and safe re-entry. Ask when people can return and when the next trade can begin.

Ask what could change the estimate. Limited access, hidden damage, wet material, or changes to the requested area can affect the final scope.

Service area

Our primary service area is Belleville, Ontario. Nearby Quinte region projects may also be considered based on location and scope. Include the property address when requesting an estimate.

Local homes range from older city properties to newer subdivisions and rural buildings. Describe the type of space so we can ask the right questions.
